metadata.description:
UPDATE (August 31, 2022): added the file parkworld.zip which is another copy of the Park World from Issue 7. It's different than the versions already in this archive. This was taken from the Virtual Reality Construction Kit book disk found here: https://archive.org/details/virtual-reality-construction-kit-software

This is a (mostly complete) reconstruction of the PCVR software though some disks are original.

What you need to know:

Issues 1-8 have been reconstructed from a vast array of VR sources and archives, 9-13 are missing entirely and 14-16 are the original disks.
This archive also includes software mentioned in the articles and in the
case of some topics, additional materials are provided to utilize
everything properly. For example, the Menelli box archive contains
everything you need and how you would've found it back then.
Consider this archive a painstaking labor of love to be used by few.
We need all disks imaged or file lists or anything related you may have.
Please share with the email at the bottom of this description.

If additional disks are discovered this archive will be updated to reflect the change. Check out Famicoman's PCVR Magainze uploads as well which now incorporate these archives. 


What you don't necessarily need to know (a deeper dive):

Confusingly, the disks don't necessarily correlate with what is in
that respectively numbered issue, hence why they're not put inside the issue folder.
For example: disk 4 doesn't necessarily accompany issue 4.
This is evident by noting that in issue 6 it's mentioned that "Disk #1"
contains REND386 v4.01. REND386 v4.01 wasn't even a thought at the time
of issue 1, v2 and possibly v3 were current at that time.

Under "Letters to the Editor" in issue 6 it mentions ""We chose
the 5.25" 360k floppy for compatibility purposes and cost.""
Using this size limit made it a bit easier to verify the contents were
complete. Some are a little over but they were packed in different ways so
this makes sense. (Weird formats like .zoo were converted to .zip but the
original file is included as well for historical purposes).

Things don't stop getting confusing there. It would appear that
PCVR took it upon themselves to rename and repackage a lot of things.
Take also into consideration other people having renamed files before uploading to
the Internet made it even more difficult to locate them by their preferred name.
Through much research I was able to find most of the originals and reconstruct others.
This is why sometimes the filenames won't be the same or the files will have
additional contents. That said, there are still files I haven't recovered,
partially due to this and partially due to the evaporation of the sacred FTP.
I urge anyone who's able to try and recover some of these files.
Which leads us to...

Call for materials:
==================
If you have the original disks from the magazines, *please*
image them and upload them or let me know and I can help you copy them.
You will be credited, if desired. 

I've tried to reconstruct everything but it's not possible. Even if I
found all the files, we'd still be missing the readme's and some other
things, and it's still not original, so please contact if you have anything or
anything related such as disks, ads, magazines, catalogs, fliers, etc.
Let's make this preservation complete!

Of particular historical importance to the preservation of VR history,
the following FTPs are missing and desperately needed:
acm.uiuc.edu
sunee.uwaterloo.ca
karazm.math.uh.edu

There are others. If you can help in some way whether it's by contacting them
or in some other way please let me know.

How to use this archive:
=======================
Any issue where anything is mentioned or was included there will be a copy of
that software where possible. This means if they were referencing a popular
demo at the time it'll (hopefully) be included here. This way we can try to
recreate the original experience entirely. While reading the magazine, if you
see something which piques your interest then I recommend looking in the
folder for that issue. 

Make sure to check the readme.txt in each folder as it contains additional
file information!

REND386 has its own folder because it's mentioned in every issue and contains
essential files. Every single version is there (except the demo, please upload)
including custom hacks and then some. It contains everything I have collected
about REND386 over two years, including every object and world I could scrounge
off of every disk and website on earth. It is THE full REND386 experience,
from the early betas to the last  release. Granted, there are still things
missing, but it is quite comprehensive. Once I dig further into my archives
I will be releasing a more comprehensive VR386/REND386/AVRIL archive so stay tuned
as it will be dropping this year (2022) here on Internet Archive.

As mentioned above, I've also included software that was mentioned in
articles but were not necessarily included on any disk. This is so that you
can utilize and experience the magazine as it was intended without having to 
hunt down the software. 

Note that you probably won't be able to simply run or compile stuff. 
It's up to you to construct an era-appropriate environment. 
Compilers have drastically changed since those days. 
Also, most of the REND386 stuff will need Borland C++ 2.0 or 3.0
to compile. It isn't included in this archive, but you can find it online. 
I recommend obtaining 2.0 through 3.0 at the least if possible to have
most/all bases covered for this archive in general since some of the code
listings need Borland C++ 2.0.
List of major version releases:
2.0 (1991), 3.0 (1991), 3.1 (1992), 4.0 (1993), 4.01, 4.02 (1994),
4.5, 4.51, 4.52 (1995), 4.53.

You can run the DOS stuff in DOSBox or VMWare but ultimately an actual
machine is preferred, especially if you're using hardware like the
PowerGlove or shutter glasses as they won't be supported (you can emulate
the Powerglove as of REND386 v3 though, I believe). If you're running in a
VM or emulator it may be way too fast so you'll need to slow it down.
These programs were generally meant to run on a 386 up to a 486/50MHz,
to give an idea of the speeds they would've originally and commonly 
been used at. The way REND386 renders, if you have a bunch of objects in
one spot everything will slow down drastically so in some cases it's good
to have more speed. This also depends on other factors such as your video
card.

Side note: check my uploads for Sean Clark's port of REND386 to Android.

Random note 1: if something seems off when you load a version of REND386,
like it's missing files or code or just doesn't work, then you're probably 
using the wrong  version. Confusingly, the articles don't always mention
which version they're using. Some of the early issues use v2,
then around issue 3 it looks like they started using v3. 
Issue 5 starts to speak about v4.

Random note 2: the first 3 issues did not include discs. 

Random note 3: Note that the disks you could order by mail weren't necessarily
the disks which accompanied the issues. Since information is scant, I've tried
to reconstruct the mail-in disks and throw in anything else mentioned where
possible. Unless we find the actual disks then it's difficult to know,
but the disks here in combination with the program listings in the
listings/ folders and the code from the articles should provide you with
pretty much the full experience except for a couple instances.

Huge thanks to Famicoman for uploading PCVR issues. I really appreciate his
efforts and it helped me reconstruct these archives.
Make sure you check out his uploads as he's included these disks with the magazines.
https://archive.org/details/@famicoman

If you have any questions you can reach out to me at vrcollect [at] gmail [dot] com
Seriously seeking all things vintage VR related. For example, I'm missing DIVE and a host
of other packages that I would like to make available to the public.
Please, let's make these things available again if you have them. You will be credited
if desired. Stay tuned to my uploads for a massive archive coming this year and contact if
interested in helping with it.
